summary: Enforce canonical scalar types and bounds in portable lease documents

delivery.outcome: Enforce the already declared scalar types, nullable references, string bounds and explicit-offset timestamps in portable lease/request/receipt validation; publish immutable standard 0.20.66. Malformed-transition receipt handling and rejected-trace anchoring remain a dependent continuation.
nonGoals: Change or deploy the effectful Subactor controller
Grant authority through local replay or alter the canonical lease schema
Mutate active foreign or frozen target work
Change transition reply format or rejected-trace semantics in this slice

architecture.decision: Use a bounded dependency-free matcher for the already shipped canonical flat scalar schema, then retain existing semantic guards. Boolean counters, invalid references and offset-free timestamps fail. Keep all transition reply and trace behavior unchanged for the dependent slice. The installed Wellman package receives the same canonical schema and byte-identical runtime through the existing bundled synchronizer; this is required distribution closure, not another behavior slice.
interfaceChanges: Run portable scalar document safety regressions in the existing Linux and Windows workflow.
architecture.rollback: Revert the material source fix through protected publication; preserve controller and review receipts.

validation.evidence: Original scalar reproductions fail; boolean counters, missing offsets, string bounds/patterns and nullable types are denied; valid offset timestamps and installed CLI validation remain supported.
Existing validator integration, parity, native gate and required exact-head Linux/Windows/OneDev checks pass.
Independent protected merge and final immutable standard v0.20.66 publication are verified.
